title: Hurco WinMax post: opt-in tool pre-fetch (T word without M06 after each tool change)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found during the tester fix round of PR #2646 (issue #2573).

**What the tester asks:** The tester's Hurco programs pre-fetch the next tool after each tool change:

```
T110 M6
T104
```

**What Hurco documents:**

- Online help, Program Functions, "M6 Initiates Tool Change": when this NC parameter is Yes (the default), a `T` word without `M06` pre-fetches the tool. The carousel moves the tool to the ready position. The change occurs at the next `M06`.
- When this parameter is No, the control ignores `M06` and a `T` word alone changes the tool.
- The 2010 WinMax NC Programming manual (704-0116-310, page 4-1) gives the same two rules.

**Why PR #2646 does not add it:**

1. The post cannot find the next tool. The engine global `programTools` (`crates/post/src/post/options.rs`) is sorted by tool number and has each tool one time. It does not give the tool-change order.
2. On a control with "M6 Initiates Tool Change" set to No, a bare `T` word changes the tool at once. The program then cuts with the wrong tool. Thus the output must be opt-in and default off.

**Proposed work:**

- Give scripts the tool-change order (for example a `toolSequence` global, or a `nextTool` value at each `TOOL` record).
- Add a Hurco option `preFetchNextTool` (default off). Write `T<next>` on its own line after `T<n> M6`. Write nothing after the last tool.
- The option description names the "M6 Initiates Tool Change = Yes" condition.

Done means: with the option on, a three-tool program writes the next tool after each `T M6`; with the option off, the output is unchanged; tests pin both.
